description.text: Summit Therapeutics Inc. (“we”, “Summit” or the “Company”) is a biopharmaceutical company focused on the discovery, development, and commercialization of patient-, physician-, caregiver- and societal-friendly medicinal therapies intended to improve quality of life, increase potential duration of life, and resolve serious unmet medical needs. The Company’s pipeline of product candidates is designed with the goal to become the patient-friendly, new-era standard-of-care medicines, in the therapeutic area of oncology. The Company’s current lead development candidate is ivonescimab, a novel, potential first-in-class bispecific antibody intending to combine the effects of immunotherapy via a blockade of PD-1 with the anti-angiogenesis effects of an anti-VEGF (as defined in Part I, Item I Business, Company Overview, Ivonescimab) compound into a single molecule. On December 5, 2022, the Company entered into the License Agreement with Akeso, Inc. and its affiliates (collectively, “Akeso”) pursuant to which the Company has in-licensed intellectual property rights related to ivonescimab (as amended, the “License Agreement”). Through the License Agreement, the Company obtained the rights to develop and commercialize ivonescimab in the United States, Canada, Europe, and Japan. The License Agreement and transaction closed in January 2023 following customary waiting periods.

analysis_md:
# SMMT — Summit Therapeutics Inc.
Engine 5.4 run, 2026-10-17. In scope: market cap $10,938,884,136.95 at $14.63 (dcf_numbers.json, nasdaq_quote_api) < $40B.

All figures below are copied from dcf_numbers.json, ttm.json / ttm.py output, financials_history.csv, or fundamentals.json — none are recomputed. Figures marked "reported" are from company releases / search results cited in this run, not from the computed outputs.

## What it is
Clinical-stage oncology biotech built around a single in-licensed molecule: ivonescimab, a PD-1/VEGF bispecific antibody licensed from Akeso in a deal that closed January 2023 — Summit holds development/commercialization rights for the United States, Canada, Europe and Japan; Akeso retains China and the rest of the world, and is owed up to $4.5B in milestones plus low-double-digit royalties (deal terms as announced at closing). The FDA has accepted the BLA for ivonescimab plus chemotherapy in EGFR-mutant NSCLC after prior targeted therapy, with a PDUFA goal date of November 14, 2026 (reported). Phase 3 evidence: HARMONi showed a progression-free-survival benefit (overall survival not statistically significant in the global readout), and HARMONi-6 in China was reported as the first head-to-head Phase 3 to show overall-survival superiority over an anti-PD-(L)1 combination regimen. A broad Phase 3 program (HARMONi-3, HARMONi-7, colorectal, bladder) is running. Post-period support: AstraZeneca agreed in 2026 to invest $2B through convertible preferred shares, and collaborations with Daiichi Sankyo and Pfizer expand the trial program (reported). There is no approved product and no product revenue.

## Owner's earnings
**FY2025 (10-K via EDGAR, from financials_history.csv):** operating cash flow -$322,930,000; capex $657,000; SBC $732,420,000 (always a real cost — and FY2025's figure is exceptional, see FLAGS).
- **Conservative owner's earnings FY2025: -$1,056,007,000 = -$1.412336232524319/share** (dcf_numbers.json: base_oe_total_latest_fy, base_oe_latest_per_share).
- **Normalized base (median of last 3 FY OE/share): -$0.2689140342068516/share** (dcf_numbers.json) — less negative only because the 2023–2024 per-share losses were smaller on a then-smaller burn; still negative.
- Maintenance version FY2025: -$1,224,474,000 (financials_history.csv) — also deeply negative; its extra depth vs the conservative figure is the FY2025 SBC / working-capital presentation, not a cleaner signal. For a company with no revenue, neither definition is close to positive; the OCF-based conservative figure is the cleaner one.
- OE positive in **0 of the last 5 fiscal years** (dcf_numbers.json: oe_positive_years_of_last_5 "0/5"), and the F sub-type is "no_cash_generation" (OCF − capex is not positive).

**Base used = TTM owner's earnings through Q2 2026, from ttm.py (filing-direct, no hand math).** ttm.py inputs quoted from ttm.json (fy_end 2025-12-31, ytd_end 2026-06-30):
- OCF: FY -$322,930,000 (period 2025-01-01 to 2025-12-31) − prior YTD -$127,912,000 (2025-01-01 to 2025-06-30) + current YTD -$263,415,000 (2026-01-01 to 2026-06-30) = **TTM -$458,433,000**
- SBC: FY $732,420,000 − prior YTD $489,880,000 + current YTD $141,497,000 = **TTM $384,037,000**
- Capex: FY $657,000 − prior YTD $422,000 + current YTD $1,154,000 = **TTM $1,389,000**
- Shares (current-YTD weighted diluted): **776,824,812**
- **TTM OE total -$843,859,000 → base OE/share -$1.086292542365395** (dcf_numbers.json: base_oe_per_share, base_source "ttm_json")
- **Every defensible base — latest FY (-$1.41), 3-yr median (-$0.27), TTM (-$1.09) — is negative. Tier F is not a base-choice artifact.**

## Moat: 3/10 — weak, and entirely contingent on approval
Justification: ivonescimab is a potential first-in-class PD-1/VEGF bispecific with Phase 3 evidence (HARMONi PFS benefit; HARMONi-6 first head-to-head overall-survival superiority over an anti-PD-1 regimen in China) and big-pharma validation (AstraZeneca's reported $2B convertible investment, Daiichi Sankyo and Pfizer collaborations), but Summit does not own the molecule — it is in-licensed from Akeso for the US/Canada/Europe/Japan against up to $4.5B in milestones plus low-double-digit royalties, Akeso keeps China and the rest of the world, there is no approved product, no revenue since 2023, no demonstrated pricing power, and returns are deeply negative. Evidence first, per the rubric: fundamentals.json's roic_proxy is negative in every year shown (2020 −3.22, 2021 −5.92, 2022 −0.19, 2023 −4.53, 2024 −0.63, as printed) and gross margin is not meaningful — revenue was $0 in FY2023 and FY2024 and no revenue was filed for FY2025. There are no through-cycle returns above the cost of capital to sit a higher score on; a 7+ score is impossible on this record.
- FOR: Potential first-in-class PD-1/VEGF bispecific — HARMONi-6 showed overall-survival superiority over an anti-PD-1 combination regimen in a head-to-head Phase 3
- FOR: Exclusive ivonescimab rights for the US, Canada, Europe and Japan under the Akeso license; BLA accepted with a November 14, 2026 PDUFA date
- FOR: Big-pharma validation and funding — AstraZeneca's reported $2B convertible preferred investment (2026) plus Daiichi Sankyo / Pfizer trial collaborations
- FOR: Broad Phase 3 program beyond the first indication (HARMONi-3, HARMONi-7, colorectal and bladder studies) — multiple shots on the same molecule
- AGAINST: The asset is licensed, not owned — Akeso retains China/rest-of-world and is owed up to $4.5B in milestones plus low-double-digit royalties on Summit-territory sales
- AGAINST: Single-molecule concentration — no approved product, zero revenue in 2023–2024 and none filed for 2025; an FDA refusal is existential
- AGAINST: No pricing power demonstrated, against entrenched NSCLC competition (Merck's Keytruda franchise and other PD-(L)1/VEGF combinations)
- AGAINST: Deeply negative returns through the whole history (roic_proxy negative every year) — no cycle-tested economics to defend
- AGAINST: Licensor dependence — supply, China data generation and the molecule's origin all sit with Akeso
- A 3 gives CAP = clamp(2 + 1.3 × 3) = **5.9 years** (dcf_numbers.json cap_years) — moot for the DCF (no positive OE to fade), but it records how short and contingent the protected window looks even in an approval world.

## DCF — 5.4 final run (2026-10-17)
Price: **$14.63** (dcf_numbers.json, nasdaq_quote_api). The engine cannot project scenarios on a negative base, and forcing one would be inventing numbers — so there are no scenario IVs or IRRs, by design (no positive normalized OE = Tier F, flagged not forced). The five scenario slots carry the default likelihoods 10/25/30/25/10 for the record, each with its story:

| Scenario | Prob | Growth start | OE mult | Story | IV@15% | IRR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Super bear | 10% | n/a — no OE base | n/a | FDA complete response letter on Nov 14, 2026; burn continues with no revenue; the equity is a wasting option on a re-file | n/a (OE < 0) | n/a |
| Bear | 25% | n/a | n/a | Approval delayed or narrow-label; launch burn extends losses for years; further dilutive raises before any positive OE | n/a (OE < 0) | n/a |
| Base | 30% | n/a | n/a | Approval occurs, but commercial and Phase 3 spend keeps OE negative for years — still no OE-DCF support today | n/a (OE < 0) | n/a |
| Bull | 25% | n/a | n/a | Clean approval, strong NSCLC uptake, HARMONi-3/7 expand the label; first positive OE late this decade — value sits beyond the OE screen's window | n/a (OE < 0) | n/a |
| Super bull | 10% | n/a | n/a | Ivonescimab displaces anti-PD-1 standards across indications — a pipeline-valuation story, not an owner's-earnings story | n/a (OE < 0) | n/a |

- **Probability-weighted IV@15% / IRR: not computable — no positive owner's earnings in any base period** (dcf_numbers.json: implied_irr_weighted null, tier_by_numbers "F", f_subtype "no_cash_generation" on the TTM legs).
- **Tier by numbers: F.** Growth sanity check per the standing rule: the engine's blended growth (-0.6008577555908065) is an artifact of the old business's revenue collapsing to zero (see BASIS_BREAK) — it describes a wound-down predecessor, not the ivonescimab program, and no scenario growth start was built on it. There are no revenue or OE prints to sanity-check a start against: the company has printed zero revenue since 2023.
- Diagnostics: TTM OE is negative, so OE yield on price is negative and effectively all of the $10.94B market cap is future/terminal option value; terminal-value share and scenario spread are not computable. reprice.py skipped SMMT by design (Tier F — no IRR exists at any price).

## FLAGS — resolving every fragility flag
The final dcf_numbers.json carries exactly six fragility flags; each is resolved here:
- **STALE_FY** (latest fiscal year ended 10 months ago): resolved by construction — the base is the TTM figure from ttm.py through Q2 2026 (ytd_end 2026-06-30), legs quoted in full under Owner's earnings. Verdict unchanged and worse in dollars: TTM OE/share is -$1.086292542365395 on a TTM OCF burn of -$458,433,000 (H1 2026 operating cash use of -$263,415,000 already exceeds the prior-year H1).
- **DILUTION** (share count growing 56.9%/yr; dcf_numbers.json share_cagr 0.5694974398082537): fires, hard, and the rate is a mixture of real financing dilution and history artifacts. Weighted diluted shares in financials_history.csv run 193,336,063 (FY2022) → 619,646,180 (FY2023) → 718,541,896 (FY2024) → 747,702,265 (FY2025) → 776,824,812 (TTM YTD). Drivers: repeated equity raises to fund the Phase 3 program (fundamentals.json records $230,482,000 of share issuance over the TTM), the pre-2021 UK-plc share basis and the 1-for-5 reverse split effective 2020-09-18 (noted in fundamentals.json), and SBC — $14,108,000 (FY2023) → $50,981,000 (FY2024) → $732,420,000 (FY2025) → $384,037,000 TTM. Expect more dilution: the TTM cash burn is funded by issuance, and even after AstraZeneca's reported $2B convertible investment, commercial launch spend lies ahead of any revenue.
- **BASIS_BREAK_SUSPECT** (>60% revenue jump/drop in the last 5 years): resolved — this is a company replacement, not a restatement of one business. The pre-2020 rows are the old UK Summit Therapeutics plc (January fiscal year-end, GBP reporting, collaboration revenue up to $57,088,000 in FY2019) whose programs were wound down; the fiscal year-end then moved to December, and the January 2023 Akeso in-license replaced the business entirely. Revenue is $0 in FY2023 and FY2024, and no revenue was filed for FY2025. Every revenue CAGR in dcf_numbers.json (5-yr −0.5508577555908064, latest YoY −0.6102819237147595) straddles that break and means nothing; none was used.
- **NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE** (net income vs operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2023, 2024, 2025): resolved year by year. **2025:** net income -$1,079,586,000 vs OCF -$322,930,000 — the gap is dominated by the $732,420,000 non-cash SBC charge, which the company's FY2025 release reconciles explicitly ($732.4M SBC vs $51.0M in FY2024, including a reported ~$651M charge from modifying employee options to remove performance hurdles — search-cited FY2025 reporting). **2023:** net income -$614,928,000 vs OCF -$76,760,000 — the year the $500M Akeso upfront was expensed through R&D on the January 2023 closing, while the cash had been largely pre-positioned in FY2022 (the FY2022 history row carries $300,000,000 of restricted cash and $514,310,000 of notes payable against that commitment), so FY2023 earnings bear an expense its operating cash flow does not repeat. **2024:** net income -$221,315,000 vs OCF -$142,106,000 — SBC of $50,981,000 plus working-capital timing explains most of the gap. In all three years GAAP net income is the distorted series; the OCF-based conservative OE used throughout is clean of these items (and SBC is then deducted in full as a real cost, which is why the OE figure is deeper than OCF alone).
- **FX_CONVERTED** (reporting currency GBP converted to USD at period-end ECB rates): noted — conversion applies only to the old plc's pre-2020 history (rates recorded in dcf_numbers.json fx_conversion, 2015–2019 fiscal years). The current company reports in USD; the FX basis touches no figure the verdict rests on.
- **DEBT_TAGS_BLANK** (no debt tag for the latest fiscal year — net debt unknown, not zero): resolved from the filing history — the company is essentially unlevered. FY2025 (financials_history.csv): total assets $751,182,000, total liabilities $92,322,000, equity $658,860,000, lease liabilities $20,890,000 (dcf_numbers.json), cash on the cash tag $225,266,000 and no borrowings outstanding; the FY2022 notes payable ($514,310,000 total) that funded the Akeso commitment are gone by the FY2024 row (debt $0).
